name: Tom hum do
summary: Vietnam Tourism calls Côn Đảo red lobster smaller than other lobsters, with firmer, sweeter meat, and the nickname fire lobster. The same account says Côn Đảo is the country’s lobster-farming kingdom and, in the next lines, that these lobsters cannot be farmed and are only caught wild. Both lines stay. Báo Điện Biên Phủ names tôm hùm on seaside menus and does not say red. No price was printed.
origin: Côn Đảo, in Vietnam Tourism. Báo Điện Biên Phủ, 31 July 2026, names tôm hùm without the word đỏ.
taste: Vietnam Tourism says firmer and sweeter meat than other lobsters.
howToEat: Vietnam Tourism says sushi, salad, soup, or steamed whole, and that a female lobster in winter may carry golden roe along the spine.
Báo Điện Biên Phủ printed no method. The farming line and the wild-only line are both on the Vietnam Tourism account. The hour is Check on arrival. No price was printed.
where: Seaside restaurants, per Báo Điện Biên Phủ. No street was printed. Check on arrival.
seoTitle: Tom hum do — red lobster in Con Dao
seoDescription: Tôm hùm đỏ is the red lobster Vietnam Tourism describes, farmed on one line and wild-only on the next. The price is Check on arrival.
